title_en: 276: Rewiring Retirement Around The World: What Can We Learn?
title_zh: 276: 全球退休制度重构：我们能学到什么？——Casey Maurer 与 Helen Lee Jones 对话
subtitle_zh: BlackRock 探讨各国退休体系变革路径与可借鉴经验
description: 276: Rewiring Retirement Around The World: What Can We Learn?

turns.en: Seven out of 10 American workers feel prepared for retirement, but what we actually see is that their own savings may translate into just 50 to 60 percent of what they actually need.
turns.zh: 七成美国劳动者觉得自己为退休做好了准备，但实际情况是，他们自己的储蓄可能只能转化为实际所需金额的百分之五十到六十。

turns.en: People around the world are living longer. That's one of society's great achievements. But it's also changing the economics of retirement. People may need their savings to last for decades, while in many countries, more of the responsibility for funding those years is shifting from governments and employers to individuals. At the same time, there is no single global model for retirement, and different countries are tackling different pieces of the
turns.zh: 全世界各地的人们寿命都在延长，这是社会的一项伟大成就。但这也正在改变退休的经济逻辑。人们的储蓄可能需要支撑几十年的花销，而在许多国家，为那些年提供资金的责任正从政府和雇主向个人转移。与此同时，并没有一个全球统一的退休模式，不同国家正在应对这个问题的

turns.en: challenge. One thing I think you can guarantee on retirement is that no two systems or two countries look the same. There's three ways to help drive particular outcomes for retirement.
turns.zh: 不同方面。关于退休有一点你可以肯定——没有任何两个体系或两个国家是一样的。有三种方式可以帮助推动退休达成理想结果。

turns.en: Help people save, how much you're saving. Two is how you translate those savings into actual investments, and then three, taking those investments and turning that into a reliable stream of income. So what can we learn from how different countries are responding? Which ideas can travel across borders and which can't? And as retirement is rewired, do we need to think differently about retirement itself? Not as a series of separate problems, but across the whole
turns.zh: 第一是帮助人们储蓄，你存多少。第二是如何把储蓄转化为实际投资，第三是把投资变成可依赖的收入流。那么我们能从不同国家的应对方式中学到什么？哪些理念可以跨越国界，哪些不行？当退休体系被重新构建时，我们是否需要用不同的方式来看待退休本身？不是把它看作一连串孤立的问题，而是从整个

turns.en: portfolio and the whole lifetime. Welcome to The Bid, where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance. I'm Oscar Pulido.
turns.zh: 资产组合和整个人生的角度来思考。欢迎来到 The Bid，我们在这里解读市场动态，探索改变经济与金融的力量。我是 Oscar Pulido。

turns.en: Joining me today are Casey Maurer, head of U.S. Defined Contribution for BlackRock, and Helen Lee Jones, EMEA head of Global Consultant Relations and Institutional Strategy.
turns.zh: 今天和我对话的嘉宾是 BlackRock 美国固定缴费（Defined Contribution）业务负责人 Casey Maurer，以及 EMEA 全球顾问关系与机构战略负责人 Helen Lee Jones。

turns.en: Together, we'll look at the forces rewiring retirement around the world, how different systems are adapting, and what those changes could mean for the future of retirement.
turns.zh: 我们将一起探讨正在重新塑造全球退休制度的力量、不同体系如何适应，以及这些变化对未来退休可能意味着什么。

turns.en: Helen and Casey, thank you for joining us on The Bid. Thank you so much for having me here, Oscar. Great to be here. Well, Helen, we're here in London. I'm visiting this week. I know this is where you're usually based. And the topic today is retirement, which is something that everybody around the world is thinking about and trying to prepare for. But it's important to take a step back and acknowledge that the way in which people prepare might vary across different regions. It might look
turns.zh: Helen、Casey，感谢你们做客 The Bid。非常感谢邀请我来，Oscar，很高兴来到这里。好的，Helen，我们现在在伦敦，我这周在这里出差。我知道你通常也驻扎在这里。今天聊的是退休，这是全世界每个人都在思考、都在努力准备的事情。但重要的是我们要退后一步，承认不同地区人们准备退休的方式可能不一样，看起来可能

turns.en: different. I guess the first question I have for you, though, is why are we talking about retirement so much today? What's changing that is bringing this topic forward in more conversations?
turns.zh: 很不同。我想问你的第一个问题是：为什么我们今天这么频繁地谈论退休？是什么变化让这个话题更多地出现在对话中？

turns.en: Well, that's a great question. And when you think about it around the world, what we're seeing right now is that the retirement systems are being fundamentally rewired. Why is that?
turns.zh: 好问题。放眼全球，我们现在看到的是退休体系正在被从根本上重新构建。为什么这么说？

turns.en: Look at the world. It's completely different. The economic, demographic, and institutional assumptions on which the old retirement systems were built no longer hold. So when you think about it, the model was that in the 20th century, you'd work maybe for 35, 40 years, maybe for the same employer, you'd retire perhaps for 10, maybe 15 years with good health, and then you receive income from the state, your employer, or both. Now, what we're seeing is that people are living
turns.zh: 看看这个世界，已经完全不一样了。二十世纪的旧退休体系所依托的经济、人口和制度假设已经不再成立。那个模式是这样的——你为同一个雇主工作三十五年、四十年，也许带着良好的健康状况退休十年、十五年，然后从国家、雇主或者两者领取养老金。现在我们看到的是人们活得

turns.en: much longer. And what we're seeing is that as those populations age and traditional defined benefit pension systems are disappearing, governments are really facing a different set of pressures, fiscal pressures, and individuals who now are increasingly accountable for their own retirement. What we're seeing right now is really a structural shift in the ecosystem. We're seeing a transfer of retirement responsibility, risk, and capital from
turns.zh: 长了很多。随着人口老龄化和传统固定收益（Defined Benefit）养老金体系逐渐消失，政府面临着一系列不同的压力——财政压力——而个人现在越来越多地要为自己的退休负责。我们目前看到的是生态系统的一次结构性转变。退休的责任、风险和资本正在从

turns.en: governments and employers all the way over to individuals. And that's really seeing a shift in the market that we're here to talk about today. And one of the things that you mentioned as to why we're talking about this is that individuals are living longer lives. This is good news, but it comes with then a responsibility to help them think about how to save and invest and also then spend in retirement. You talked about greater responsibility on that individual in terms of
turns.zh: 政府和雇主全面转移到个人身上。这正是我们今天想讨论的市场变化。你提到为什么我们在讨论这个话题——一个原因是人们活得更久了。这是好消息，但随之而来的是帮助人们思考如何在退休期间储蓄、投资和消费的责任。你谈到个人在管理退休投资方面更大的

turns.en: managing those investments in retirement. And Casey, if I could come to you then for a second, what does it mean when we're talking about individuals having to take more of that responsibility? How is that changing what retirement systems are having to do on behalf of these investors? First, Oscar, I think it forces us to rethink what success actually looks like in retirement systems. As responsibility shifts more to individuals,
turns.zh: 责任。Casey，我来问你——当个人必须承担更多责任时意味着什么？退休体系正在如何改变为这些投资者提供的服务？首先，Oscar，我认为这迫使我们重新思考退休体系中成功到底是什么样子。随着责任更多地转向个人，

turns.en: we're asking people to make pretty complex financial decisions at different points throughout their life. And when we think about the phase in particular, for example, where someone is approaching retirement, often this is where their own financial picture looks the most complex.
turns.zh: 我们在让人们在人生的不同阶段做出相当复杂的财务决策。尤其当我们想到临近退休的那个阶段，往往这个时候个人财务状况看起来最复杂。

turns.en: And kind of overnight, we're asking people to be part actuary, part investor, part financial planner. And that is a tall order. One of those questions as well is how long do my savings need to last for me? So not only is that a tough financial question to answer, it's also deeply personal.
turns.zh: 几乎一夜之间，我们要求人们一半是精算师、一半是投资者、一半是财务规划师——这个要求太高了。其中一个问题是'我的储蓄需要支撑我多长时间'，这不仅是一个很难回答的财务问题，也是极其个人化的问题。

turns.en: When I think about what resonates with me with retirement, and one of the reasons I'm so passionate about this work is when I was growing up, my parents knew that they would have the traditional defined benefit pensions. One was a teacher, one was a military pilot, and what that gave them, and really us as a family, was a sense of security about that time and their lives. And I think the reality of this is it's less common nowadays. As responsibilities just to individuals, I don't
turns.zh: 说到退休让我产生共鸣的地方，也是我对这份工作如此充满热情的原因之一——我小时候，父母知道他们会有传统的固定收益养老金。一个是老师，一个是军用飞行员，那给了他们——也给了我们整个家庭——一种关于那个阶段的安心感。但现实是，这种保障如今越来越少了。既然责任转到了个人身上，我并不

turns.en: think this means that we just leave individuals to their own. I think there's a real role to play for our policymakers, for the financial services industry, for employers to really help reduce the complexity that individuals may face some of those questions that we talked about, and really help solve for outcomes. If we think about retirement as the freedom to do what comes next, then I think what success looks like is not the size of someone's retirement account, but actually
turns.zh: 认为这意味着我们就把个人放任不管。我认为政策制定者、金融服务行业和雇主都有真正的角色要扮演——帮助减少个人面对的复杂性，帮助我们讨论的那些问题得到解答，真正实现目标成果。如果我们把退休定义为'做接下来想做的事情的自由'，那么我认为成功不是退休账户的规模，而是

turns.en: it's help in providing that certainty, that security to do just that, to be able to allow them to do what's next. And Helen, Casey sits in the US, and maybe she's thinking about retirement through a little bit more of a US lens. You're based here in the UK. You work a lot with savers and investors across the broader European continent. What does retirement look like in parts of the world, like the UK and Germany? Are there differences in those approaches? And is there anything that
turns.zh: 帮助提供那种确定性和安全感，让人们真正能够去做接下来的事。Helen，Casey 在美国，可能她思考退休更多是从美国视角出发。你驻扎在英国，与整个欧洲大陆的储蓄者和投资者打交道很多。在英国、德国这些地方的退休是什么样的？那些方式有什么不同？有没有什么

turns.en: is going on in those countries that we can learn and maybe apply in other parts of the world? One thing I think you can guarantee on retirement is that no two systems or two countries look the same. And really, when you look at the UK, it's going to fundamentally different place to Germany.
turns.zh: 是我们可以从这些国家学到并可能应用到世界其他地方的？关于退休有一点你可以肯定——没有任何两个体系或两个国家是一样的。你看英国，跟德国是完全不同的地方。

turns.en: The UK system is really a market-based retirement system. It's got a range of different pension savings options, whereas Germany is really a principally state-led pay-as-you-go system.
turns.zh: 英国的体系是一个以市场为基础的退休体系，有各种各样的养老金储蓄选项，而德国基本上是一个以国家主导的现收现付（pay-as-you-go）体系。

turns.en: Maybe if we just bring that to life through some numbers, the OECD puts the UK pension provider asset industry at almost $3 trillion. Compare that to Germany, and that's almost $300 billion, because our population sizes are pretty equivalent. In the UK, there's 70 million people.
turns.zh: 也许我们用一些数字来具象化。经合组织（OECD）估计英国养老金行业的资产规模接近3万亿美元。相比之下德国只有大约3000亿美元，因为我们的人口规模相当接近。英国有七千万人。

turns.en: In Germany, there's around 85 million people. But the pensions industry is not even a tenth of the size of the UK. And so that really shows you how much of the pension provision is being provided by the state rather than by the kind of commercial or pension savings industry.
turns.zh: 德国有大约八千五百万人。但养老金行业甚至不到英国的十分之一。这说明了多少养老金实际上是由国家提供的，而非商业或养老金储蓄行业。

turns.en: But I think other really important piece to note is that they're in fundamentally different starting points. We could look at the UK and say, wow, what a great success story. There's $3 trillion of retirement assets. The UK has never really had a state-funded pensions industry. It's really moved into the hands of the employer and the commercial sector since almost the 1950s. The UK system has really advanced over many decades. And really what we're now seeing in the UK is
turns.zh: 但我认为另一个真正重要的点是它们处于完全不同的起跑线上。我们可以看英国说'哇，多成功的案例，有3万亿美元的退休资产。'英国从来没有真正有过国家资助的养老金体系。从大约1950年代起就交给了雇主和商业部门。英国的体系已经发展了几十年。我们现在在英国真正看到的是

turns.en: that system that has been in the hands of companies to provide for their employees through defined benefit systems. It's now moving into defined contribution. They're almost in the kind of third age of pension provision from state to fully corporate funded to now corporate provided in terms of platform and defined contribution. But really the responsibilities falling to the individual. And when you look at what's happened in the UK, regulation has really kind of triggered
turns.zh: 那个曾经由企业通过固定收益体系为雇员提供保障的系统，现在正在向固定缴费转移。它们几乎处于养老金供给的第三个阶段——从国家到完全由企业出资，再到现在由企业通过平台提供固定缴费方案。但责任真正落到了个人身上。当你看英国发生了什么时，监管实际上触发了

turns.en: a lot of that innovation. You go back to 2012 with the introduction of auto-enrollment where employers really had to provide a mandatory pension saving system for their employees.
turns.zh: 很多创新。回到2012年自动注册（auto-enrollment）的引入，雇主必须为员工提供强制性的养老金储蓄体系。

turns.en: It's massively increased the amount of employees, the amount of savers into retirement systems to almost 90 percent of eligible workers, which I think is a huge success of a regulatory change here in the UK. Because Germany has had such great success in providing for pensioners in retirement through a state-funded system, the impetus to change hasn't really been there.
turns.zh: 这大幅增加了进入退休体系的储蓄者数量，达到合格员工的近百分之九十，我认为这是英国一次监管改革的巨大成功。因为德国通过国家资助的体系在保障退休人员方面已经非常成功，变革的动力一直没有真正出现。

turns.en: But when we go back to the beginning of our conversation talking about those changing economic and demographic shifts, that kind of shift towards needing to rethink the system I think is increasing across many parts of Europe and around the world. But what we are seeing from Germany is that there is a shift perhaps towards a little bit of the individual retirement responsibility. There's going to be some reforms coming in at the end of this year where we'll see
turns.zh: 但回到我们开头谈到的那些经济结构和人口结构的变化，那种需要重新思考退休体系的转变正在欧洲许多地方、全世界范围内加速。但从德国我们看到的是，正在向个人承担更多退休责任的方向转变。今年年底将会有一些改革落地，届时我们将看到

turns.en: the creation of a capital market-based retirement product, which will really put the responsibility for investing into the hands of individuals even more so than it was before.
turns.zh: 一种基于资本市场的退休产品的诞生，这将把投资责任更多地交到个人手中。

turns.en: So when you think, what are we learning from these two markets? I think there are really three things to take away. It's not a slow game, right? Retirement reform takes decades. This plays out over a really long time frame. I think the second thing to really note is that employer participation is really critical unlock to helping individuals save for their retirement.
turns.zh: 那么我们从这两个市场学到了什么？我认为有三点需要记住。第一，这不是一个快过程，对吧？退休改革需要数十年，这是一个非常漫长的时间跨度。第二，雇主的参与是帮助个人为退休储蓄的关键突破口。

turns.en: It's much easier to help investors save if it's a default in your corporate pension plan than having to convince millions of savers to go ahead and buy a financial investment product.
turns.zh: 在企业养老金计划中把储蓄设为默认选项，比去说服数百万储蓄者主动购买一个金融投资产品要容易得多。

turns.en: And then maybe the third story, and that's really related to the size of the UK system, is that gaining access to capital markets and staying invested in capital markets over the long horizon is really the critical part of having larger asset pools that can provide for people in their retirement. Yeah, just on those last points, it sounds like the more you make it convenient for people to save for retirement, the more you provide them access to capital markets,
turns.zh: 第三个启示和英国体系的规模有关——进入资本市场并在很长的时间维度里持续投资，是拥有更大资产池、能为人们退休提供保障的关键所在。好的，就你说的最后这几点，听起来越让人们方便地储蓄、越为他们提供进入资本市场的渠道，

turns.en: that's beneficial to them. But there is that theme of the individual having to take responsibility, perhaps the days of somebody's going to do it for you are starting to go away and you have to do it more yourself. And Casey, perhaps to then come back to you, where in the US, there's been a tremendous amount of success over the years with 401ks, where individuals are saving and investing for themselves. They've done a great job of helping
turns.zh: 对他们就越有利。但确实有这么一个主题——个人必须承担责任，也许有人替你做这一切的时代正在远去，你不得不更多自己动手。Casey，我们回到你——在美国，401(k) 在过去这些年取得了巨大成功，个人通过它为自己储蓄和投资。401(k) 很好地帮助人们

turns.en: people accumulate savings. But what is that next phase of the 401k look like as people are aging and moving into retirement? And as you say, they want the freedom to do what's next. I think it builds on actually some of what we just talked about. But the history of the 401k gives us a great blueprint when we think about what could come next. One clear lesson is that plan design really matters. And I think this is a timely conversation because in August, we just passed
turns.zh: 积累了储蓄。但当人们步入老龄、进入退休阶段时，401(k) 的下一个阶段是什么样的？就像你说的，他们想要做接下来想做的事的自由。我觉得它实际上建立在我们刚才讨论的一些基础上。401(k) 的历史给了我们一个很好的蓝图来思考下一步。一个清晰的教训是方案设计真的很重要。我觉得这是一个很应时的对话，因为八月我们刚刚走过了

turns.en: the 20 year mark since the Pension Protection Act in the US. And what this did is helped accelerate some really important innovations in the marketplace. So things like automatic enrollment, investment defaults like target date funds. And so I think it's important to pause for a minute there and actually say this is a success story. There are some really successful innovations when we think about retirement systems. And oftentimes, when we're having this conversation
turns.zh: 美国《养老金保护法案》（Pension Protection Act）出台20周年的节点。这部法案帮助加速了市场上一些非常重要的创新，比如自动注册、投资默认选项、目标日期基金（target date funds）。我觉得值得停下来花一分钟说——这本身就是一个成功故事。退休体系确实有一些非常成功的创新。通常我们讨论退休时聚焦于挑战，那很重要，

turns.en: about retirement, we focus on the challenges. And that is really important. But I think the opportunity now is to just build on that success. As you said, build on that accumulation system and really think about how we can help people achieve particular outcomes. This is important because there's still a gap. Our own research from read on retirement survey that we do every year tells us that seven out of 10 American workers feel prepared for retirement. And that's pretty good.
turns.zh: 但我觉得现在的机会是在成功之上继续建设。就像你说的，在积累体系基础上，真正思考如何帮助人们实现特定的成果。这很重要，因为差距仍然存在。我们每年做的 Read on Retirement 调研显示，七成美国劳动者觉得自己为退休做好了准备——这其实还不错。

turns.en: But when we layer on our own research, what we actually see is that their own savings may translate into just 50 to 60% of what they actually need. That's a shortfall of about half.
turns.zh: 但当我们叠加我们自己的研究，实际情况是他们的储蓄可能只能转化为实际所需金额的百分之五十到六十。这差不多是缺口一半。

turns.en: And that doesn't mean the 401k has fallen short. Let's be clear. It just means the evolution is not over. And so I think we need to do two things. One is help people make those savings work harder for them. What's exciting is there's a lot of innovation and creativity and value that the industry is bringing to help people achieve this. And then the second is turning those hardworking savings and investments into a reliable stream of income. And so I have a lot of optimism about this
turns.zh: 这并不意味着 401(k) 失败了，这点要明确。只是说进化还没有完成。所以我认为我们需要做两件事：一是帮助人们让储蓄更有效地为他们工作。令人兴奋的是行业正在带来很多创新、创造力和价值来帮助人们实现这一点。第二是把那些努力工作的储蓄和投资变成可依赖的收入流。我对此非常乐观，

turns.en: because we're not starting from scratch and we don't need to reinvent the 401k. We just need to finish the job. And one of the things that you mentioned in the US is this need to address retirement income and help people also have a paycheck in retirement. There's another market in the world very far from the US but similarly tackling this retirement income challenge which is Australia. I'd love to hear a little bit more about what you see there and then maybe to contrast
turns.zh: 因为我们不是从零开始，我们不需要重新发明 401(k)，只需要把这项工作完成。你提到在美国需要解决退休收入问题，帮助人们在退休期间也有一份薪水。世界上还有一个离美国很远的市场也在应对退休收入这个挑战，那就是澳大利亚。我想多听听你在那边的观察，然后也许再对比一下

turns.en: that with a region of the world like Latin America where there it's more about expanding access to markets. What are some of the observations in these different regions and what does it tell us about the evolution of the retirement system around the world? Yeah, Oscar, I think one of the most important lessons and Helen touched on this earlier is there's not a single model that works everywhere. Different systems are tackling different parts of the retirement challenge.
turns.zh: 像拉丁美洲这样的地区——在那里更多是关于扩大进入市场的机会。这些不同地区有什么观察？它们告诉我们全球退休体系的进化是什么样的？好的，Oscar，我认为最重要的教训之一——Helen 之前也提到了——就是没有一个放之四海而皆准的模式。不同体系在解决退休挑战的不同方面。

turns.en: And what we just talked about in the US, for example, is the innovations we've seen have made it much easier for many working Americans but we're still working through how to translate those savings into income. And then Australia, as you mentioned, is interesting because what we can see is that they are further along in tackling income. They've built up huge retirement pools of assets through superannuation funds and they're turning to their focus to how they can then
turns.zh: 我们刚谈到的美国，比如我们看到的创新已经让很多美国工薪族更容易了，但我们仍在解决如何把储蓄转化为收入。澳大利亚，就像你提到的，很有趣，因为我们可以看到的是他们在应对收入方面更超前。他们通过超级年金（superannuation）基金建立了巨大的退休资产池，现在正转向如何把那些

turns.en: translate that to help support people through retirement, balancing things like longevity and flexibility throughout. Mexico I think is another interesting example and what fascinates me is they're tackling two sides of the equation. So one, increasing the amount that people save and then two, the actual investments that are powering those savings and using things like target date structures to help do that. I think stepping back what this is telling us is that there's three
turns.zh: 转化为帮助人们安度退休，平衡长寿性和灵活性等各个方面。墨西哥我认为是另一个有趣的例子，让我着迷的是他们同时在解决两个方面的方程。第一，提高人们的储蓄量，第二，推动储蓄的实际投资，使用目标日期结构来帮忙。我想退后一步看，这告诉我们的是有

turns.en: ways just to simplify it to help drive particular outcomes for retirement. One is help people save, how much you're saving. Two is how you translate those savings into actual investments and what's powering that. And then three, taking those investments and turning that into the reliable stream of income. And all three matter. The reality is no single market has the answer that works for all. And one of the reasons I find the retirement story globally so interesting is that, like I
turns.zh: 三种方式来推动退休的理想结果。第一是帮助人们储蓄——存多少。第二是如何把储蓄转化为实际投资，什么在驱动它。第三是把投资变成可依赖的收入流。三者都重要。现实是没有任何一个单一市场有适用于所有人的答案。我觉得全球退休故事如此令人着迷的原因之一是，就像我

turns.en: said, different systems are solving for different parts of it. But I do believe that good ideas travel, countries can learn from each other. And at the same time, no market is exactly the same.
turns.zh: 说的，不同体系在解决不同的部分。但我确实相信好的理念可以传播，各国可以互相学习。同时，没有哪个市场是一模一样的。

turns.en: And finally, given that, we know it's very local at the same time. It's a very universal human experience. And so I think the combination of learning across markets, remembering what we're actually trying to solve for at the human level while coupling that with local implementation is really, really critical. The good news is that there seems to be evolution going on around the world. And that looks different in different regions. And like you said, a very local type of
turns.zh: 最后，正因为如此，我们知道它是非常本地化的。但它也是非常普遍的人类体验。所以我认为跨市场学习、记住我们在人类层面真正要解决的问题，同时结合本地化实施，这是非常非常关键的。好消息是全球各地似乎都在发生进化。不同地区看起来不同。就像你说的，非常本地化的

turns.en: solution depending on the population, the region that we're talking about, whether it's more addressing retirement income or just expanding access to capital markets. And so Helen, it's clear there are different ways to solve for this puzzle. As these retirement systems evolve though, how does the industry need to adapt with them? And what does it mean to think about retirement more holistically across the whole portfolio and the whole lifetime?
turns.zh: 解决方案取决于人口、取决于我们谈论的地区——是更多解决退休收入问题还是仅仅扩大进入资本市场的机会。所以 Helen，很明显解决这个问题有不同的方式。随着这些退休体系不断演进，行业需要如何适应？从整个投资组合和整个人生的角度更整体地思考退休意味着什么？

turns.en: That is a great question, Oscar. And I just love those examples that Casey brought to live around the innovation we're seeing in Australia and in Mexico and the US. And I think that diversity is just a huge opportunity. And every time you see a market change, there's an opportunity for innovation.
turns.zh: 好问题，Oscar。我特别喜欢 Casey 举的那些例子，关于我们在澳大利亚、墨西哥和美国看到的创新。这种多样性就是一个巨大的机遇。每次你看到一个市场变化，都有一个创新的机会。

turns.en: And personally, I find that really exciting. And yes, I think pensions can be exciting. And I think we're here on a mission to try and build excitement around the pension's opportunity for individuals. Because joking aside, I think one of the challenges and opportunities for the industry is that we've got to demystify a lot of the perceived complexity and anxiety around saving for retirement. And when you look at the ecosystem as it stands today, it's really been built
turns.zh: 就我个人而言，我觉得这真的让人兴奋。是的，我觉得养老金可以让人兴奋。我们在这里的使命之一就是尝试围绕养老金为个人带来的机会建立热情。说笑归说笑，我认为行业面临的挑战之一也是机会，就是我们得去祛魅围绕退休储蓄的那些复杂感和焦虑感。当你看当前的生态系统时，它实际上是建立在

turns.en: for the same needs. It's just been advising corporates and governments to build pension plans rather than individuals. So when you look at that ecosystem, and you mentioned the whole portfolio, whole of life opportunity set, you could take that real institutional knowledge and convert it into something that makes sense for the individual. So think about that in real terms. What does that mean? It means financial panic, not only in your retirement, but to and through retirement. It also
turns.zh: 服务同样的需求之上——只是它一直在为企业和政府提供咨询来建设养老金计划，而不是为个人服务。所以当你看那个生态系统，你提到了全组合、全生命周期的机会，你可以把那些真正的机构知识转化为对个人有意义的东西。从实际意义上想想这意味着什么。它意味着财务上的安心——不仅仅是在退休时，而是在通往退休和贯穿退休的过程中。它还

turns.en: means looking at things like new and creative investment products. So rather than having to build complex asset liability, matching models and thinking about how to really ensure corporates can provide for pensioners in their retirement, it's really about designing investment solutions that do that for you. So think about investment products that provide income or investment products that help draw down or spend your capital responsibly through a period of time in your
turns.zh: 意味着关注新型创意投资产品。不是非得去构建复杂的资产负债匹配模型，思考如何确保企业能在退休后为退休人员提供保障，而是真正去设计能够为你做到这一点的投资方案。想想那些提供收入的投资产品，或者那些帮助你在退休期间负责任地提取或消费资本的投资产品。

turns.en: retirement. And then I think there are a whole host of other things that are happening around the individual and around the industry, which probably are a little bit more behavioral in nature and auto-enrollment, I think is a good example of that, where you're really seeing prompts and reducing the friction of decision-making coming into play. So automatically putting employees into pension-saving systems, automatically increasing your contributions to your pension as your earnings
turns.zh: 退休期间。然后我认为围绕个人和行业正在发生的很多事情，可能更多是行为层面的——自动注册就是一个好例子，你真正看到的是减少决策摩擦的提示机制在发挥作用。自动把员工纳入养老金储蓄体系，随着你的收入增加自动提高你的缴费比例，

turns.en: increase, I think those types of systems and those types of evolutions in the market are going to be some of the most important things that we'll see evolving over the next decades and centuries to come, I'm sure. When I take a step back and really think about what's happening, we're really seeing a blurring of the boundaries between institutional and individual investment ecosystems. And I think in the past, you would have seen them as two very separate spaces. But that blurring, I think,
turns.zh: 我认为这类体系和这类市场进化将是我们未来几十年甚至几个世纪里看到的最重要的演变之一。当我退后一步真正思考正在发生什么时，我们看到的其实是机构投资和个人投资生态系统之间边界的模糊。过去你会把它们看作两个非常独立的领域。但这种模糊，我认为

turns.en: is really meaning that saving for your retirement is no longer a singularly defined moment. It's almost moving from saving for retirement to just saving for a range of different life outcomes.
turns.zh: 真正意味着为退休储蓄不再是一个单一定义的时刻。它几乎正在从'为退休储蓄'转变为'为一系列不同的人生目标储蓄'。

turns.en: And I think increasingly that's going to be, as Casey mentioned, a really interconnected set of choices that individuals are going to need to make over a whole lifetime. And what does that mean for the ecosystem around it? For the financial services industry, it really means that we've got to be thinking through how to help individuals make the best decisions at every step of that journey along the way. And I think part of the blurring of those lines is historically we've
turns.zh: 我觉得越来越多地，正如 Casey 提到的，那将是一组高度互联的选择，个人需要在整个人生中做出。这对周围的生态系统意味着什么？对金融服务行业来说，真正意味着我们必须思考如何在旅程的每一步帮助个人做出最佳决策。我认为这种边界模糊的一部分在于，历史上我们

turns.en: talked about defined benefit plans and defined contribution plans. And we've used some of that terminology here in this discussion. And I think part of what's happening is that some of those benefits of the pension, the defined benefit plan, professional management, retirement income access to broader opportunities, I think some of that is coming to the defined contribution space as well, Casey, if I understand correctly, where the individual still has ownership,
turns.zh: 一直在谈固定收益计划和固定缴费计划。我们在这次讨论中也用了这些术语。我认为正在发生的一部分是，养老金——固定收益计划的一些优势，专业管理、退休收入、更广泛的投资机会，我觉得其中一些正在进入固定缴费领域。Casey，如果我理解正确的话，个人仍然拥有所有权，

turns.en: but is getting some of those benefits. Is that type of personal pension part of the next evolution of retirement? I absolutely think so. When we think about the defined benefit plan and what traditional pensions do so well, it is exactly what you just said. It's pooling the risk. It's the professional investment management with a broad toolkit. It's that, in many cases, paycheck for life. And then the DC plans bring different strengths. They have the ownership and portability
turns.zh: 但同时获得了其中一些好处。这种个人养老金是否是退休的下一次进化的一部分？我绝对这么认为。当我们想到固定收益计划和传统养老金做得好的方面，恰恰就是你刚才说的——风险共担、专业投资管理、广泛的工具箱、很多时候是终身的薪水。而固定缴费计划带来了不同的优势：个人所有权、可携带性和

turns.en: and flexibility. And that's really important. And so to me, the idea of the personal pension is bringing some of those best features of the defined benefit plan into the modern retirement system and the defined contribution space. And so this connects back to an idea I was talking about earlier, this sense of security that my parents had. And so while this may look different for many now and in the future, we shouldn't give up on trying to provide that same confidence.
turns.zh: 灵活性，这些都很重要。所以对我来说，个人养老金的理念就是把固定收益计划的一些最佳特性带入现代退休体系和固定缴费领域。这让我回到我之前谈到的一个理念——我父母那种安全感。虽然现在和未来对很多人来说可能看起来不同，但我们不应该放弃提供同样的信心。

turns.en: And so I think that's what makes this idea so compelling. It's not about creating systems of the past, but actually taking features of the defined benefit, things like guaranteed income, things like private markets, where it makes sense to help power those investments, and actually bringing them into the defined contribution space to preserving those things that we all enjoy in that space, the flexibility ownership like we talked about. With this, I
turns.zh: 所以我认为这就是这个理念如此有吸引力的原因。它不是要复制过去的体系，而是把固定收益的特点——比如保障收入、私募市场（private markets）等适合帮助驱动投资的东西——真正带入固定缴费领域，同时保留我们在固定缴费中享受的一切——灵活性、所有权，就像我们谈到的。随着这一切，

turns.en: think it's important and Helen touched on this a little bit as well. We have to remember that with that increased sophistication or complexity, that all has to stay under the hood. We as an industry have to absorb that complexity and can and are for the individual. I think that's really key as well.
turns.zh: 我认为很重要的一点——Helen 也提到了——我们必须记住，随着复杂性的增加，所有那些都必须藏在引擎盖下面。我们作为行业必须为个人去吸收那些复杂性，而且正在这样做。我认为这一点非常关键。

turns.en: And that's a great point. I think sometimes we talk about it a lot on the bid, which is financial markets can be complex, and we're trying to demystify a lot of these topics. And retirement can be complex if you want it to be complex, but the industry is really trying to simplify and create more convenience for the end investor. Anytime we've done an episode on retirement, listeners will know that I sometimes reference my own parents who are retired. And when I think
turns.zh: 说得好。我觉得我们在 The Bid 上经常讨论这个——金融市场可以很复杂，我们正试图为很多话题祛魅。退休也可以很复杂，如果你想要它复杂的话，但行业真正在努力的是简化和为最终投资者创造更多便利。每次我们做退休相关的节目，听众都知道我有时会提到我自己已经退休的父母。当我想到

turns.en: about what is it that gives me comfort is they have peace of mind. They took good steps in an era before the system had evolved as much as it's evolving now. And so it sounds like from listening to both of you that around the world, there's a lot of evolution going on in retirement systems and is setting up a good foundation for more people to have this sort of peace of mind that my parents seem to have right now. Helen and Casey, thank you so much for sharing this global
turns.zh: 什么让我感到安心的是——他们内心平静。他们在体系还没有进化到像现在这样程度的年代做了正确的步骤。所以听起来你们两位说的，全球退休体系正在发生大量进化，正在为更多人建立这种我父母现在似乎拥有的内心平静的基础。Helen、Casey，非常感谢你们分享这个关于退休的全球

turns.en: perspective on retirement. I'm sure we're going to be talking about this topic for many, many years to come. And thank you for doing it here on the bid. Thanks Oscar. It's been a real pleasure to be here. Thanks Oscar. It's been fun. Thanks for listening to this episode of the bid. Next up, Alex Brasier and Kerry King join me to discuss what's behind the recent strength in equity markets, how investors are thinking about AI and market concentration,
turns.zh: 视角。我相信这个话题我们未来还会讨论很多很多年。谢谢你们来到 The Bid。谢谢 Oscar，真的很荣幸来到这里。谢谢 Oscar，很有趣。感谢收听本期 The Bid。下期节目，Alex Brasier 和 Kerry King 将与我讨论近期股市走强的原因、投资者如何看待 AI 和市场集中度，

turns.en: and where opportunities may be emerging across global equities as we look toward your end. Don't forget to subscribe to the bid wherever you get your podcasts.
turns.zh: 以及在全球股票中可能出现哪些机会。别忘了在你收听播客的平台订阅 The Bid。
